reason: The c-file pin permits quiet moves on the file, but Mine forbids capturing c8. Sideways moves expose c1.
Only e2-g2 blocks the checking g8 rook. The e4 capture and all other rook moves leave g1 checked.
Mine restricts captures, not geometric attacks. The f8 rook still attacks f1/f2 and forbids short castling. e2 is friendly-occupied.
Every knight landing square is enemy-occupied. Inspecting the knight must not grant a capture; the king can still move.
b5-c6 is en passant even though c6 is empty; b5-a6 is an ordinary capture. Both are forbidden by the triggered Mine.
En passant vacates b5 and exposes the b1 king to b8. Removing a Mine debuff cannot legalize that move.
Mine allows every quiet promotion and forbids every capture-promotion. Promotion does not replace the piece identity.
The mined rook can participate in quiet castling. f2 is friendly-occupied; neither route is attacked.
